name: MongoDB
description: Protects against destructive MongoDB operations like dropDatabase, \ dropCollection, and remove without criteria

destructive_patterns.name: stdin-unverified
destructive_patterns.description: mongosh receives indirect input that the engine cannot statically verify.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize and review the exact JavaScript before piping or redirecting it into mongosh.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-database
destructive_patterns.description: dropDatabase permanently deletes the entire database.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
dropDatabase() removes the current database completely:

- All collections are dropped
- All indexes are removed
- All documents are gone
- Users scoped to the database lose access

This cannot be undone. The database can be recreated but data is lost.

Backup first: mongodump --db=dbname --out=/path/to/backup

List databases: show dbs

destructive_patterns.name: drop-collection
destructive_patterns.explanation:
drop() removes the entire collection:

- All documents are deleted
- All indexes are removed
- Schema validation rules are lost
- Cannot be undone

Backup collection first: mongodump --db=dbname --collection=collname

Count documents before dropping: db.collection.countDocuments()

destructive_patterns.name: delete-all
destructive_patterns.description: remove({}) or deleteMany({}) deletes ALL documents. Add filter criteria.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
An empty filter {} matches ALL documents in the collection:

- deleteMany({}) removes every document
- remove({}) (deprecated) does the same
- Collection structure and indexes remain

If you want to delete everything, drop() is faster. Otherwise, add filter criteria: db.collection.deleteMany({ status: 'expired' })

Preview what would be deleted: db.collection.countDocuments({}) // All documents! db.collection.find({}).limit(10) // Sample docs

destructive_patterns.name: mongorestore-drop
destructive_patterns.description: mongorestore --drop deletes existing data before restoring.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
mongorestore --drop drops collections before restoring them:

- Existing data is deleted first
- If restore fails partway, data may be lost
- Only affects collections being restored

Safer approaches:
- Restore to a different database first
- Use --nsExclude to skip certain collections
- Remove --drop and handle conflicts manually

Test restore: mongorestore --db=test_restore --drop /backup/path

destructive_patterns.name: collection-drop
destructive_patterns.explanation:
db.<collection>.drop() is the most common way to delete a collection:

- All documents in the collection are deleted
- Indexes on the collection are removed
- Cannot be undone

Before dropping: db.collection.stats() // Size and document count db.collection.find().limit(5) // Sample documents

Backup: mongodump --db=mydb --collection=mycollection
